Oliver Glasner has frequently highlighted Forest’s poor running data but in the first-half here their heat maps will have been electrified.

Forest have scored their first goal at the City Ground since the final game of last season. That is a drought of almost eight and a half hours.

City then establish some possession, with Gvardiol advanced and playing inside Doku in a narrow position.

Evangelos Marinakis, the Forest owner, is at the City Ground today in his first appearance of the season.

Marinakis has been busy with his various other business interests but is here this evening.

As a very superstitious man, can his return bring Forest some good fortune?

Just like the lyrics of Forest’s Mull of Kintyre-inspired pre-match song, there really is a mist rolling in from the Trent on a crisp autumnal evening.

Remembrance Day will be marked just before kick-off.

Even a City win today will have them three points behind Arsenal for the international break.

The margins for error are very small in title races and who knows how damaging those two successive league defeats could be for Enzo Maresca.

There is, of course, their feud with the Premier League over the guilty verdict for breaking financial rules which could render everything irrelevant.

Very warm reception for Elliot Anderson from the Forest fans as he runs to the tunnel leading to the dressing rooms.

Anderson was at Forest for two seasons before that £116m move to Manchester City.

Man City will be hoping to close the gap on Arsenal to three points at the top of the table after the north London side’s 1-0 win over Hull City this afternoon.

While matters off the pitch may suggest otherwise, on it, City look the most likely side to deny Mikel Arteta’s men a second successive league title.

The two teams currently share the same goal difference (10), but City have conceded twice as many goals as Arsenal, something Maresca will be hoping to address.

From the current top eight in the league, only Chelsea have conceded more.

Forest are yet to score at home in any competition this season and have netted only six league goals in total from an xG of 14.34.

That underperformance of 8.34 goals is the biggest of any team in the Premier League this season, and of any side after nine Premier League games since at least 2021-22.

Forest come into this evening’s game in 19th, but they are just a point behind Crystal Palace and Manchester United, while victory would also take them above Coventry City and up to 16th.

Forest’s results at the City Ground have to improve quickly or this team will be in serious trouble.

They have gone almost eight and a half hours without scoring in front of their own supporters.

Forest have only recorded two home wins in the Premier League over the past 11 months which, quite frankly, is relegation form.

Oliver Glasner has played down the significance of his warning to Nottingham Forest’s squad after their defeat at Brentford has had the desired impact.

The Austrian said last weekend there would be “no compromises” and insisted his players have to fully buy into his philosophy.

Speaking this week, he said: “I didn’t attack anyone directly. We share that we want to be successful and win games. It was not a problem.

“It was much louder outside than I felt it was inside. This is just how I see a relationship has to be. Let’s talk about things if we don’t like things.

“If you never say anything in your relationship with your wife or children, then they will never know. Then I can’t blame somebody because if they don’t know, how can you expect things to change?

“We are now in a society where criticism or the way I talk is negative, but the intention was positive and to change to get better results so that we can all have a better life.”

Gianluigi Donnarumma, who has made three errors leading to goals this season, “recognises that he has made some mistakes,” Enzo Maresca said this week, “but at the same time recognises that he has made some great saves”.

The City manager added: “It is quite easy with him because he recognises any mistake immediately. I’ve spoken to him about it, but I didn’t feel the need to be so deep with him because he already knows and recognises that he has made some mistakes.”

Asked about City players adapting to his philosophy, Maresca said: “I can see my playing style just by working every day with them, but we can still improve many things.

“We know exactly what we are doing well and what we need to improve. It is just a matter of time.”

Elsewhere this afternoon, Martin Odegaard has broken the deadlock at the Emirates to give Arsenal a 1-0 lead over Hull City.

Victory would take Mikel Arteta’s side six points clear of City at the top of the table before this evening’s contest at the City Ground.

With around 10 minutes remaining in north London, you can follow our updates of that match here.

Erling Haaland will be hoping for his 10th league goal in 10 games this term, having bagged nine from nine so far.

Last week’s 1-0 defeat against Brighton was the first league game he failed to score in since the opening match of the season against Bournemouth.

The Norwegian is once again leading the way in the Premier League’s scoring charts, with three goals more than his nearest rivals.

Oliver Glasner pressed the nuclear button last weekend and the big question today is how his Forest players respond.

After the 2-0 defeat at Brentford, Glasner warned there would be “no compromises” and insisted his players have to fully buy into his philosophy.

This usually goes one of two ways and Glasner will be hoping it produces a positive reaction.

"If they don't want to follow, I guess the sixth manager will come in." Oliver Glasner is ready to make some changes at Nottingham Forest. https://t.co/xiCCA25IV4

Training has apparently been excellent this week but it will mean little unless they transfer it into a match situation.

James McAtee has been Forest’s best player so far this season and faces the club he joined as an 11 year old.

Enzo Maresca made a flawless start at Manchester City but is now enduring a stumble.

Two successive Premier League defeats have seen City replaced at the summit by Arsenal, so the importance of this match has gone up a notch.

Elliot Anderson returns for the first time since his £116m move from Forest in the summer and what a signing he already appears.

Forest are already wondering whether their asking price should have been higher and, as daft as it sounds, City have probably got a bargain.

There will be a lot of focus today on goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, who has been unconvincing in recent weeks.

Maresca has made three changes following City’s 3-2 win at Leipzig in midweek, with Dias, Gvardiol and Doku replacing Nunes, O’Reilly and Foden.

Our line-up to face Forest! 👊🩵 XI | Donnarumma, Khusanov, Dias (C), Guéhi, Gvardiol, Anderson, Fernández, Ndiaye, Cherki, Doku, Haaland SUBS | Rulli, Kovačić, Reis, Nunes, Bouaddi, O'Reilly, Allan, Foden, Lewis 🤝 @etihad https://t.co/1N9iOorlpb

Glasner has made two changes to his Forest team following defeat at Brentford last weekend, with Yates and Munoz replacing Ndoye and Aina.

Is this the day the xG gods reward Nottingham Forest? Oliver Glasner’s team sit 19th having won one game all season, but there is no doubt that their performances have been significantly better than results and they might need their luck to turn against Man City team full of firepower.

Despite all of the positive indicators in Forest’s underlying data, Glasner caused some alarm with his comments after last weekend’s defeat at Brentford.

The Austrian said: “We have to accept it’s not good enough. If we lose four of the last five games, it’s not good enough. And that’s why for me, it’s now time that we change things, that I change things, and that’s what I will do.

“I feel now maybe I made too many compromises in some stuff, and it’s always compromises. It’s a clear way. I will tell [the players] what we want to do, what we have to do, and if the players buy in, I think we can have a turnaround, and if not, the sixth manager [since the start of last season] will come in.”

Dangerous words perhaps when you work for Evangelos Marinakis, but John Percy reported this week that Glasner was backed by his players in a squad meeting.

City are smarting from back-to-back defeats by Aston Villa and Brighton, but they created more than enough in both games to claim some sort of result. Nevertheless, there is a persistent sense that their defensive unit remains too marshmellow-like over the course of 38 games, and Forest have the counter-attacking threat to test them.

Glasner has happy memories of playing City, beating them in the 2025 FA Cup final with Crystal Palace, but his Forest reign is in urgent need of a signature victory and performance.

#1034. Medicinal plants, lessons from mushrooms and the power of smell: Books in brief

Andrew Robinson is a writer based in London and author of Earthshock (1993), The Story of Measurement (2007) and Einstein in Oxford (2024).

Margaret Willes Bodleian Library Publishing (2026)

According to ancient Greek medical authority Hippocrates, “Nature itself is the best physician” — hence the title of writer Margaret Willes’s appealing book. Introduced with a substantial essay on European herbalism from medieval times to the present, it discusses 100 plants with medical properties, from alecost (Tanacetum balsamita, a member of the daisy family) to the yew tree (Taxus baccata). Each is illustrated with an exquisite colour drawing taken from John Gerard’s 1597 The Herball, or Generall Historie of Plantes.

When motor cars were invented in the late nineteenth century, their emissions were welcome at first, because they replaced the odour of horse dung that had reduced many city streets to “a state of organic olfactory crisis”, notes historian William Tullett. His engrossing history of smell ranges from ancient Christian aromas, through medieval Indian perfume and the scents of eighteenth-century slavery to the status of odour in twentieth-century China. It features “the foul, the fragrant, and everything in between”.

Jim Al-Khalili Princeton Univ. Press (2026)

Just before his death, Albert Einstein stated: “the distinction between past, present and future is only a stubbornly persistent illusion”. In this compelling, if intellectually demanding, book about the physics of time, physicist and broadcaster Jim Al-Khalili disagrees. He argues that “the irreversible passage of time needs to be incorporated into the laws of physics”. By comparing the concepts of time in quantum mechanics, the general theory of relativity and thermodynamics, he concludes that time’s arrow is real, and makes the Universe tick.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03595-x

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Where do you want to live? Cultured Amsterdam? The beautiful old city of Udine, near Venice? Or Sunderland?

We sincerely don't mean that as a slam on the north-east town, either.

After all, that's the decision young Danish goalkeeper Thomas Sorensen faced when deciding his next career move back in 1998 - and he picked the move to Wearside.

Sorensen told FourFourTwo: "I have my parents to thank for that.

"I was talking to a few clubs, like Ajax and Udinese, who had a long history of Danish players.

"Then this left-field offer came in from Sunderland. I hadn’t heard a lot about them and I sort of dismissed it.

"My mum and dad told me to go over and have a look. I was blown away.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

"I knew that this was the right thing for me. I would get an opportunity to play, I loved the feel of the northeast and their passion for football.

"It was probably one of the best decisions I ever made. "

Sorensen does admit that he had to adapt a little bit to Peter Reid's unique management style, however.

He said: "I had to get used to all the swearing!

"He was a great manager. One of the old school. He was probably the last manager I had who would allow the players to go out and have a few drinks.

"He cherished that camaraderie. He really encouraged the players to spend a lot of time together and that was probably part of our success.

"He said things as they were. He could be quite tough, but he was fair."

#1031. What postdoc ads ask for and what they leave unsaid

Wenhuan Xu is a postdoctoral researcher at Simon Fraser University in Vancouver, Canada, working on global change and environmental health.

Around the globe, less than one-third of postdoctoral-level job listings provided a salary range, whereas nearly half asked for collaboration experience.Credit: vicky_81/iStock via Getty

I did not start reading postdoctoral-researcher job adverts because I wanted to analyse academic-labour hiring practices. I started because I needed a job.

As my postdoc in forestry at Simon Fraser University in Vancouver, Canada, neared its end in October, I found myself looking for another position. Some evenings, I would sit with too many browser tabs open: one job in the United Kingdom, one in Canada, another in Germany, all of which promised exciting science. I was looking for a project that matched my training, a laboratory group whose work I admired and a city that I could imagine living in.

But after a while, I began to see a pattern. The adverts were often clear about what institutions wanted from me, but remarkably vague about what they were offering in return. This was never just a professional puzzle. My wife and I have four children, so salary, contract length, relocation costs, visa issues and childcare are not abstract details — they determine whether a move is even possible.

A 60-minute guide to landing your next job in science

A 60-minute guide to landing your next job in science

To better understand this imbalance, I started systematically collecting data from the ads. In 2024–26, I compiled 7,846 research-job adverts from seven international job boards (LinkedIn, jobs.ac.uk, Times Higher Education Unijobs, Nature Careers, EURAXESS, Science Careers and EuroScienceJobs). From those data, I identified 2,896 postdoc-equivalent listings across 53 countries. What had felt personal looked different at scale. (Nature’s Career columns are editorially independent of the Nature Careers jobs board.)

Around half of those nearly 3,000 listings were in Europe and roughly one-quarter were in North America. Asia, Africa and Oceania represented much smaller shares of the postdoc pie. I also scanned each ad for seven practical terms: salary range, contract length, pension, health insurance, visa support, parental leave and relocation assistance. The amount of information that each region was willing to share with applicants differed starkly (see ‘Says little, asks a lot’). Ads from Oceania disclosed these details most often. European ads, despite dominating the job boards, revealed much less on average. Ads from Asia and Africa divulged the least.

That does not mean postdocs are necessarily better supported in one region than another. It means that the information available at the point of application is systematically uneven. For someone considering an international move, that matters. My family and I were genuinely weighing up different futures: returning to Asia (I am from China and have been in Canada since 2018), moving to Europe or staying in North America. When a listing omitted salary or contract length, I was not just missing data — I was lacking the information needed to assess rent, childcare, immigration and whether a move was truly practical. In my own job search, this was immensely frustrating.

For each serious opportunity, I made a one-page comparison sheet. I began with the advertised salary and contract length, then checked the university’s published pay scale and, if I could find it, the relevant collective agreement between the institution and a union. Housing needed a more-local comparison than a city-wide average: I first looked at whether the university offered accommodation for staff or postdocs, then compared its price and availability with rentals close to campus and in nearby non-university neighbourhoods.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-02903-9

#1030. Chelsea one of three clubs keen on Arsenal star Martin Zubimendi for January transfer

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

The defensive midfielder has fallen out of favour under Mikel Arteta and could be available to move in the January window

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid and Chelsea are monitoring Arsenal’s Martin Zubimendi ahead of a potential January move.

The three clubs all have a need for a midfielder, and the Spanish international is viewed as one of the few of a high level potentially available in the next window.

Having initially been a fixture in Mikel Arteta’s midfield after a long-awaited £60m move from Real Sociedad in the summer of 2025, Zubimendi fell out of favour towards the end of last season’s title run.

The Arsenal manager still sees him as a valuable option in a midfield where he likes having a number of potential configurations, but the squad now has an abundance of options in that area after the £85m purchase of Bruno Guimaraes in the summer.

Arteta has been using the Brazilian and Declan Rice as his primary midfield two of late, with Myles Lewis-Skelly oftern in the mix as well, and that comes as he also intends on bolstering a comparatively thin forward line in the summer.

Arsenal want a transitional winger – a fast player who can carry the ball up the pitch quickly – but are unlikely to move without first making a major sale.

That is what has led the two Madrid clubs and Chelsea to feel a deal may be possible for Zubimendi, who is seen as making the most sense as an outgoing.

Should that be possible, it would be expected Arsenal want to recoup the £60m at least.

Despite falling out of favour, Zubimendi was still a key player in a title season, and played a significant part in the Ferran Torres goal that won Spain the World Cup in July.

The Spaniard is currently wearing a protective mask while he plays after suffering a suspected broken nose during the closing stages of Arsenal’s 2-0 win over Everton last month.

Having come on as an 80th minute substitute, Zubimendi took a blow to the face and required treatment – but has been deemed fit enough to play, while donning the facewear as the injury heals.

#1029. Sky pledges backing for Equal Sport Project

Sky Sports is proud to support the Equal Sport Project, which is aiming to accelerate progress towards equality across sport through five shared ambitions; the project launches at a time when women’s sport is experiencing unprecedented momentum, yet significant inequalities remain

Sky Sports is proud to support Equal Sport Project, which aims to accelerate progress towards equality across sport through five shared ambitions.

The Equal Sport Project unites sport in the UK behind five shared ambitions for women and men across sport - from local leisure centres to the biggest stadiums, and from grassroots pitches to boardrooms.

Major sporting organisations from across the UK's sporting landscape - including the FA, RFU, Youth Sport Trust, England Netball, UK Sport, LTA, Women's Sport Trust, Women in Sport, Team GB and Sport England - have made specific pledges to drive progress and help turn these ambitions into reality. Brands and broadcasters are also playing their part, signalling growing support for the movement across the wider sporting industry.

The rest of the industry is also being asked to commit support and pledges as the project seeks to gain momentum in the months and years to come.

The project launch comes at a time when the momentum of women's sport has never been stronger; participation is growing, audiences are growing and investment is accelerating.

But it also recognises that progress remains deeply uneven and that significant inequalities remain across all areas of the sporting system - from community and school sport right up to the highest levels.

Research published earlier this year by Sporting Insights found that fewer than 1 per cent of women working in sport believe gender equality has been achieved across the industry, while more than half believe they are paid less than men for carrying out the same role.

Women's sport also continues to receive a disproportionately small share of media coverage, accounting for around 9 per cent of broadcast sports coverage on key channels and 8 per cent of prime-time sports coverage. Meanwhile, gendered attitudes are increasing, with 41 per cent of boys agreeing some sports are for boys and nearly two-thirds (64 per cent) of girls want to be more active; confidence, body image, unequal facilities and gender stereotypes continue to present barriers to participation.

Accepting that there are already myriad priorities across the sector, The Equal Sport Project has identified five specific areas where collective leadership, investment and action will have the greatest impact and calls on the entire system to align behind them.

This project is a call to action, which Sky is proud to support.

"For more than 30 years, Sky has backed women's sport," Sky Sports CEO Johnathan Licht wrote on LinkedIn.

"Today, we're the UK's leading investor in women's sports rights, investing in its growth and giving female athletes a platform on the biggest stage."But visibility is only part of the story. Lasting change means breaking down the barriers that prevent girls from having the same opportunities to play, participate and stay in sport."Our Game Changing research found that girls in the UK miss out on 280m hours of sport every year. That's a gap we're determined to help close."That's why I'm proud that Sky is pledging its support to the Equal Sport Project. We'll continue to use our investment, platforms, partnerships and insight to grow women's sport, while going beyond broadcasting to create more opportunities for girls to participate."Through initiatives including the Alessia Cup and our wider Game Changing work, we're focused on turning visibility into participation and helping create lasting change for women and girls in sport."There's much more to do, and more to come from us on this soon. Collaboration across the industry will be critical if we're going to break down these barriers and close the gap."

#1028. Liverpool’s expensive attack feast on Palace to leave Sage looking doomed

Crystal Palace are playing this season as if afflicted by a curse. They seem to have made a terrible deal, possibly involving a monkey’s paw. As a result, Pierre Sage’s team were able to defend credibly for around 44 minutes of each half, on one condition: They must switch off completely, at least twice per game.

This being the Premier League, those lapses in concentration are usually punished. A mostly compact performance out of possession briefly became as porous as a bath sponge when Liverpool eased into a 2-0 lead, nine minutes after half-time. Florian Wirtz did not even need to finish cleanly to score his first Premier League goal of the season, striding on to an unopposed low cross from Bradley Barcola and killing the match as a contest.

Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz combine to put Liverpool 2-0 up! 🔴 https://t.co/F6sw33FkYZ

Major signings need to lay down a marker when arriving at Liverpool. Barcola has his hat-trick at LASK in the Champions League, but we are still waiting for a stirring big-match-defining contribution from him since his summer arrival. Arguably the same could be said for Wirtz, nearly 18 months since he joined.

Neither left Selhurst Park looking like the world-beaters they did occasionally for their previous clubs. Still, one misfiring attacker creating a goal for another represents progress and all great partnerships must start somewhere. Lennon and McCartney would improve after 1958’s Too Bad About Sorrows.

If there was ever a place for the least-productive expensively assembled attacking group in the league to find form it was surely south London on this Sunday lunchtime. Liverpool came in with two defeats in their previous two but, European trophy aside, it has been a lousy 2026 for Palace.

They have the most defeats of any ever-present Premier League team and began (and ended) the weekend with the worst defensive record. They have conceded twice as many goals from headers as any other team. Even their most loyal fan group has disbanded.

Alexis Mac Allister opened the scoring in gut-punching fashion, after a series of Palace near-misses. Chairman Steve Parish rubbed his face in the directors’ box, in the style of peak-stress era Guardiola. None of this looked good for Sage, who appears on the brink of dismissal, with Thomas Frank his most likely replacement.

Asked if he expected to remain in his job on the other side of the international break Sage said he deemed his prospects “better than you, I think”.

“We deserved better today,” the Frenchman said. “But football is not about what you deserve it is about how efficient you are and today we had a lack of efficiency”.

Counter-intuitively, it was Palace’s flashes of promise which suggested the Frenchman might be doomed. There is enough to work with here, and plenty going marginally against Palace to suggest a change in leadership might prompt a turnaround, however unfair it would be on their manager. Yéremy Pino hit the bar, Jorgen Strand Larsen had his composed close-range goal struck from the record by VAR, Daichi Kamada stung Alisson Becker’s palms and the Brazilian saved well again from Adam Wharton’s feathered header.

Jorgen Strand Larsen thought he had the opener against Liverpool, but it was ruled out for offside! ❌ https://t.co/JkSKbtkvak

The other factor which seems likely to condemn Sage is his team’s boneheaded defensive lapses. Liverpool were awarded a debatable free-kick out wide, Quinten Timber let Mac Allister run off him too easily and he duly nodded Dominik Szoboszlai’s delivery past Dean Henderson with ease. Another header conceded.

Liverpool have taken the lead against Crystal Palace thanks to Alexis Mac Alister's header! 💥 https://t.co/kNal7qsQ35

Mac Allister, formerly of Brighton, endeared himself to the Holmesdale Road Stand with a priggish celebration. There was some blowback from the seats closest, but a more dominant sense of resignation. Someone in the adjoining block took out their phone and snapped a picture. Formerly hated rival scoring against you, rubbing it in with his celebration: truly one to show the grandkids.

Liverpool had put together little of substance until then, with Wirtz drifting through another half, Alexander Isak looking keen but flawed and Barcola spooning a promising shot into low-Earth orbit. The second half was better, but Isak looked to have wasted his best chance, a one-on-one with Henderson thumped too close to the goalkeeper.

Isak had his moment in the end, checking back to finish calmly at the end of a counter-attack against a tiring defence. Eight for the season for him and an assist for Wirtz, too, although it was hardly a pass of Molbyesque majesty.

“Happy for him,” Iraola said of Wirtz, also praising Isak’s movement for the German’s goal. “I think [Wirtz] has been very unlucky in the Premier League, a couple of goals disallowed and situations where he deserves honestly to score.”

So it was Liverpool’s blip righted here, despite all of Palace’s pressure. Alisson, who took some flak for his performance at Fenerbahce, was hard to fault. He may not have reached Eddie Nketiah’s stoppage-time penalty, but made a series of brave saves and deserved a clean sheet. For all that attacking talent, the long-serving goalkeeper still looks like one of Iraola’s most important players.

13 - Liverpool have earned more points away from home in the Premier League this season than any other side (13). It's the Reds' joint-most ever from their first five away matches of a league campaign. Journeymen. https://t.co/lFe8MO3T6m

FULL TIME: Brighton's fine start to the season continues after a comfortable win against ten player Brentford, Florian Wirtz bags his first goal of the season as Liverpool inflict more pain on Crystal Palace, Bournemouth edge past Ipswich at Portman Road to continue their fine form and Sunderland pick up a huge win at home to Chelsea!

Liverpool condemn Palace to a fourth successive Premier League defeat. Mac Allister, Wirtz and Isak were all on target for the visitors, before Nketiah netted a last-gasp penalty. This result leaves Palace rooted to the bottom of the table following Sunderland’s win over Chelsea, while Liverpool move up to fourth. Will this end up being Sage’s last game in charge of Palace?

Finally, Alisson is beaten. Nketiah steps up and slams a confident penalty into the net. The Liverpool goalkeeper dives the correct way, but can’t keep it out as his clean sheet disappears. Palace’s attacking efforts have deserved a goal.

There’s a clash of heads in Liverpool’s penalty area as Kerkez and Osorio both challenge for the ball. The Hungarian catches the Palace attacker and he’s late, so the referee points to the spot.

Following that goal, Isak is withdrawn and replaced by Koumas. There’s four minutes of added time to end this game.

A good day but a middling performance from Liverpool. A goal for Wirtz, an assist for Barcola, and now Isak doing his bit for the revival narrative. Contributions from three of the most criticised members of Liverpool’s expensively-assembled attacking group. Not sure we will be seeing a great deal more of Pierre Sage in the Selhurst Park dugout.

Game, set and match for Liverpool. The visitors break as Munoz whips a cross into Wirtz, who has the composure to play in Isak. The striker cuts inside of a desperate challenge before smashing a clinical, close-range effort into the roof of the net. Palace fans flood out of Selhurst Park. Henderson makes a goal-saving stop. Mitchell fails to deal with a high clearance and Munoz pounces on the mistake before teeing up Isak. The Liverpool striker is through on goal, but Henderson does brilliantly to block his one-on-one effort. Sage makes a late double change as Khalaili and McNeil replace Mingueza and Pino.

Wirtz tests Henderson with a whipped attempt following Nyoni’s strong run and Munoz’s lay-off. However, the Palace captain makes a simple save.

Munoz tries to dribble away from Lerma, but the Liverpool substitute dives over the Palace man’s outstretched leg. Mac Allister then unnecessarily squares up to Lerma because of his annoyed reaction to Munoz’s simulation. As a result, all three of the aforementioned players are booked.

Palace can’t find a way past Alisson. Osorio drives down the wing and picks out the unmarked Pino, whose shot is smothered by the Liverpool goalkeeper. Lerma latches onto the loose ball, but Alisson is there once again to comfortably gather the Palace man’s ambitious rebound.

Liverpool continue to protect their two-goal advantage and make another forward change as Ngumoha comes on for Gakpo.

Sage makes an attacking change as Nketiah, who scored the winner against Liverpool at Selhurst Park in September 2025, replaces Strand Larsen up top.

In fairness to Palace, you can’t fault their effort. Liverpool are holding firm and the hosts are lacking end-product. Pino then catches Araujo with a late tackle to pick up a needless booking.

No need to be dramatic, but this does rather feel like the season for Pierre Sage. Losing games you have created the best chances in is a bad look for a manager under pressure, especially in the specific circumstances Palace are displaying. Iraola makes a double change as Nyoni and Munoz replace Szoboszlai and Barcola.

Alisson claims Wharton’s cross as Strand Larsen falls on the Liverpool goalkeeper. The Brazilian has been faultless today and looks well on the way to a deserved clean sheet as things stand.

Sage makes a change on the hour-mark as Osorio replaces Timber in the game’s first alteration.

Barcola is booked after halting a Palace counter with a forceful challenge through the back of Pino.

That second Liverpool goal has left Selhurst Park very deflated. All the noise is coming from the away fans. Mitchell’s makes a crucial intervention to block Barcola’s cross. Palace look so stretched now.

It’s an excellent team goal as two of Liverpool’s big-money attackers devastatingly combine. Barcola is released down the wing and finds Wirtz with a low, pinpoint cross. The German playmaker then sweeps a composed, first-time effort into the bottom corner, leaving Henderson rooted to the spot. It’s a wonderful finish and credit to Barcola for the assist. Palace are in trouble and have a mountain to climb.

Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz combine to put Liverpool 2-0 up! 🔴 https://t.co/F6sw33FkYZ

Palace have made a positive start to this second half. They win the ball high up the pitch and Kamada tees up Strand Larsen. The striker has a shooting chance, but his touch lets him down, allowing Jacquet to come across and make a tackle.

Timber slides a pass in behind Jacquet for Strand Larsen to chase. However, Alisson is alert to the danger and rushes off his line to collect possession.

We are back under way at Selhurst Park. Both sides are unchanged at the break. Can Palace find a way back into this contest?

A thoroughly entertaining first half at Selhurst Park comes to a close as Liverpool hold a slender 1-0 lead over Palace thanks to Mac Allister’s 40th-minute header. Palace struck the bar through Pino and had a Strand Larsen goal ruled out for offside, but Liverpool have also looked dangerous going forward and their opener came as no surprise to anyone. To Palace’s credit, they’ve really taken the game to Liverpool so far, forcing Alisson into a couple of notable saves. However, there was still boos at half-time and Sage has work to do.

Much fury and gnashing of teeth towards the referee Tony Harrington at half time. The tunnel entrance takes players and officials past some of Palace’s most vociferous fans and several were giving him their most strident opinions.

Anger mostly towards the free kick which led to the goal, but it didn’t seem too egregious a decision to me.

Score is very harsh on Palace, though with Kamada, Strand Larsen and Pino all coming desperately close. Exactly the sort of hard luck story you’d expect from a team in trouble.

We lead at the break 👊 #CRYLIV https://t.co/7e9WF0j1KA

Despite Szoboszlai’s enforced absence and Liverpool’s numerical disadvantage, Barcola leads an attack that creates a shooting opportunity for Wirtz, which is blocked by Disasi. There will be three minutes of added time at end this first half. There’s a break in play as Szoboszlai is down and in need of treatment.

Alisson produces another sensational stop. A teasing cross is glanced towards goal by Wharton, whose header is parried away by the diving Liverpool goalkeeper. Alisson has been in inspired form so far this afternoon.

Liverpool have taken the lead against Crystal Palace thanks to Alexis Mac Alister's header! 💥 https://t.co/kNal7qsQ35

Palace score but the offside flag is up! Liverpool fail to clear a Palace corner as Mingueza finds Pino with a clipped cross. The Spaniard fires the ball across goal and Kamada diverts it into Strand Larsen’s path. From close range, the striker chips into the net and rushes to the corner flag to celebrate. Szoboszlai swivels and tries to find Wirtz with an intricate pass. The German playmaker made a darting run into the penalty area, but Wharton was there to make a pivotal sliding interception.

The Palace bench jump up and the home players rush to the referee, who pulls out a yellow card. Araujo’s tackle was reckless and dangerous. It’s right on the verge of a red, but he escapes that punishment. The Liverpool defender needs to be careful now.

Palace strike the bar! The hosts make a rare foray forward as Mitchell finds Pino with a pinpoint cross. The Spaniard weaves into some space between two Liverpool defenders and slams a powerful half-volley against the woodwork.

Szoboszlai hangs a deep cross towards the back post. Gakpo directs it back across goal with a first-time volley, but no Liverpool has the attacking instinct to take a chance and anticipate it. Isak was instead loitering near the penalty spot. The visitors are well on top here.

Palace have been careless in possession so far, prompting groans from the home support. Szoboszlai draws a save from Henderson with a bobbling long-range strike, forcing the Palace captain into conceding a corner.

Liverpool are popping the ball around with real intent as Gakpo clips a teasing cross into Barcola. It’s just out of the winger’s reach, with Barcola claiming he was pushed by Mingueza. After seeing the replays, the Palace man just eased the Frenchman off the ball. There was minimal contact. Fun start. Barcola the first example of a player obeying Iraola’s advice to go down more, collapsing from a gentle push after climbing for a header he was never like to reach. It’s been a fast-paced and frantic start to this game. Isak’s delightful touch takes him away from Disasi, who pulls the Liverpool forward to the ground, giving the visitors a free kick. The Palace defender is perhaps lucky to avoid a yellow card for that foul.

Mitchell lashes a dangerous delivery across the six-yard box towards Strand Larsen, but solid defensive work from Van Dijk and Araujo allow Liverpool to clear.

Barcola lofts a ball over the top of Palace’s backline for Isak to latch onto. However, Disasi recovers well and blocks the Liverpool striker’s fierce half-volley from a tight angle.

A loose pass at the back from Palace gifts Liverpool an early opportunity, but Henderson does well to get down low and gather Mac Allister’s low, fizzing effort from outside the penalty area.

Liverpool get us under way at Selhurst Park. Can Iraola inflict more misery on Sage?

This is my second visit to Selhurst since the Holmesdale Fanatics ultras group decided to hang up their large drum and all-black outfits. The atmosphere is noticeably less fierce. A pretty meek rendition of Glad All Over greets the players as they come out of the tunnel, althoiugh it is hardly the sort of rabble-rousing song to strike fear into an opponent at the best of times. Now you will experience the full power of the Dave Clark Five.

The whole of Selhurst Park observes a minute’s silence to remember those who lost their lives in war.

The Palace and Liverpool players are out on the pitch. Both sides are looking to return to winning ways in the Premier League before the international break.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League match between Crystal Palace and Liverpool at Selhurst Park.

The pressure is building on Palace head coach Pierre Sage, who desperately needs a win to lift the mood and propel the club out of the relegation zone. Nottingham Forest’s impressive 3-1 win over Manchester City on Saturday evening means that Palace have dropped to a lowly 19th and are two points from safety. To make matters worse, Sage’s beleaguered side have also conceded the most goals in the division (21 in nine games).

On Thursday night, Daichi Kamada’s stoppage-time equaliser rescued a 1-1 home draw in the Europa League against Hoffenheim, after Palace delivered an alarmingly lacklustre performance.

Meanwhile, Liverpool also endured midweek European torment, as Andoni Iraola’s men fell to an error-ridden 3-2 defeat away at Fenerbahce in the Champions League, having previously lost 1-0 to Arsenal in their most recent Premier League encounter on Merseyside last weekend, which has left the club in sixth but just five points behind second-place Man City.

Speaking to reporters on Friday, Iraola said: “I think that’s the challenge, especially in a club like Liverpool. One week ago in this same press conference, we were on a run, everything was in a good place and we were in a better mood. And now, two defeats, it changes. It has to change and it has to be like this in a club like ours. Now we have to react after two defeats.”

As for Palace’s team news, Jean-Philippe Mateta is serving the first match of a three-game domestic ban after he was sent off for Palace in the 2-0 defeat to Tottenham last time out in the league. Liverpool’s long-term absentees include Hugo Ekitike, Giovanni Leoni, Conor Bradley and Jeremie Frimpong, while Ryan Gravenberch could also miss out after struggling with a heel injury.

Mauricio Pochettino has been linked with the soon-to-be vacant Manchester United position repeatedly for the best part of 10 years

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

In a revealing sit-down with FourFourTwo last year, USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino has finally lifted the lid on a legendary encounter with Sir Alex Ferguson, a meeting that has fuelled a decade of what-ifs at Old Trafford.

The Argentine, who took the reigns of the US national side on a contract running through until 2030, recounted how the most successful manager in British history once sought him out.

“Through the secretary of the League Managers Association, Sir Alex asked for my phone number so that we could have lunch," Pochettino told FourFourTwo.

"It was a meeting in London between colleagues, between a genius and an apprentice.”

The lunch, which took place some years ago during Pochettino’s tenure at Tottenham Hotspur, has long been cited as the moment Manchester United first identified him as their long-term successor.

Despite those historic links which persisted through his stints at Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea, the stars never quite aligned for Pochettino to take the hot seat in Manchester.

The USMNT boss shared a charming anecdote from the afternoon that proved it's not just his footballing tactics that are up to scratch, it's trivia, too.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

“When we asked for the bill, I wanted to take it, and so did he. We started arguing over who’d pay!

"He said, ‘Stop Mauricio, I’m going to ask you a question. If you answer correctly, you pay. If not, I’ll pay.’

"He said, ‘Name an Argentine player who scored in the 1930 World Cup final.’ I replied, ‘Stabile.’ He couldn’t believe it. The name came to me out of nowhere! In the end, I paid the bill.”

Despite his current focus, having led the USMNT at their home World Cup earlier this year, Pochettino has freely admitted he would like a return to the Premier League some day.

"Right now it’s about enjoying the World Cup," he said. "After that, I’ve always said I came so close to winning the Premier League and Champions League, and want to try again. I’d like to be part of a project with the ambition of winning both."

Pochettino’s comments are especially relevant as Man United face what looks to be another period of transition.

Michael Carrick is expected to be relieved of his duties at Old Trafford during November's international break. For now, the self-proclaimed 'apprentice' remains on the international stage, but the pull of a Premier League return is unmistakable.

Pochettino's USMNT take on Haiti in a Concacaf Nations League double header this month.

Mauricio Pochettino's full interview with FourFourTwo is available in print issue 391.

Joe takes a keen interest in youth football, covering PL2, U21 Euros, as well as U20 and U17 World Cups in the past, in addition to hosting the industry-leading football recruitment-focused SCOUTED podcast. #1026. Arsenal eye four targets to boost attack including highly rated Bournemouth star

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Mikel Arteta is keen to add a transition player to his front line

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Arsenal are looking at Alex Baena, Endrick, Antonio Nusa and Junior Kroupi as potential winger signings, should they make a move in January.

Mikel Arteta wants to bolster his attack with pace after summer movement that left his forward line thin, but any deal is likely dependent on an outgoing.

There is an obvious contrast in midfield, where he has a range of options, which means a number of clubs - including Real Madrid, Atletico Madrid and Chelsea - feel a deal for Martin Zubimendi may be possible.

Should that happen, Arsenal would be expected to use the money to buy a wide player, with Arteta wanting a transition player who can carry the ball up the pitch at pace and also be effective in tight spaces.

Kroupi is the ideal candidate, but it is seen as unlikely that Bournemouth do a deal until the summer.

Arsenal are consequently surveying options, with Atletico's Baena, Real Madrid's Endrick and Leipzig's Nusa seen as potentials.

The potential availability of Zubimendi could also give Arsenal further leverage, since both Atletico and Madrid want him. A swap isn't considered impossible, while that still allows Arsenal to move for Kroupi at a later date.

#1025. McTominay had heart 'shocked' two days before Scotland's World Cup opener

The 29-year-old missed Sebastien Pocognoli's first camp as he recovered from heart surgery; Scotland host North Macedonia on November 13, with their final Nations League game away to Switzerland three days later

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Scott McTominay has revealed he needed to have his heart “shocked” two days before Scotland's World Cup opener against Haiti.

The Napoli midfielder underwent a cardiac ablation procedure in Manchester in September to treat a mild, benign heart arrhythmia that first came to light after the Scots arrived in the United States in early June and then continued to affect him in August while back in Italy playing for his club.

At the time, the Scotland camp, clearly keen to keep McTominay's situation under wraps, said the 29-year-old had missed training in the lead-up to the World Cup due to a stomach complaint.

But, speaking at a press conference at Hampden on Tuesday, the former Manchester United player said: "I had to go and get the shock on my heart two days before the Haiti game."

McTominay played all three of Scotland's matches at the World Cup but struggled to hit the heights as his team exited at the group stage.

"I was 100 per cent (fit), but obviously when you're sat in a hospital bed two days before the first game of the World Cup about to get put to sleep, it's not ideal, is it?" he said.

"You've prepared so well, I was in such good condition and then something like that happens and you're thinking, 'How is this happening to me?'

"It's nowhere near an excuse, but it's something that you have to look back on and say, 'Well, it's part of the process'.

"Obviously, with the way the World Cup went, it was at least two, three weeks of me sitting there disappointed, not quite with it mentally. I needed time to settle down and have a break.

"After the World Cup, it was probably the most disappointed I've ever been in my career.

"I'm always one for a glass half full, but that one took a good couple of weeks to get out of my system."

McTominay returned to action with Napoli at the start of this season, but after playing their first two Serie A matches, he decided surgery was the only option and duly spent all of September on the sidelines after undergoing a corrective procedure.

That meant he missed Scotland's first four matches under new boss Sebastien Pocognoli, but he is now back with the national team for this month's Nations League double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland after featuring in all nine of his club's matches since the last international break.

"I'm good. I'm feeling much, much better than what I was," he said. "I feel like it was something that needed to be done. In your career you have moments like that where things can take you a bit by surprise.

"Obviously, it looks a lot worse to people in the media and family and friends who reach out to you after they've seen news relating to a heart issue. But it was a relatively straightforward procedure which went really, really well in Manchester.

"I'm just really happy to be back playing football again. That's the most important thing in my life and it always will be."

#1024. Bournemouth star gets first England call-up after Ezri Konsa blow

Please refresh the page or navigate to another page on the site to be automatically logged inPlease refresh your browser to be logged in

Konsa has been ruled out of Thursday clash with Croatia at Wembley, leading James Hill to be called up as a replacement

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Bournemouth defender James Hill has been called up to the England squad for the first time, with Ezri Konsa being ruled out of Thursday’s Nations League game against Croatia.

Arsenal star Konsa will not be available for the World Cup rematch with Croatia at Wembley in another hit to Thomas Tuchel’s defensive options, following the withdrawal of Marc Guehi, although it is hoped the 29-year-old will be back in contention to face Spain in Madrid on Sunday.

That has prompted Tuchel to give 24-year-old Hill, who has impressed for Bournemouth last season and has become a even more important member of a flying Cherries side this term, a maiden call-up.

A statement released by England said: “AFC Bournemouth defender James Hill has received his first call up to the England squad. The 24-year-old, who represented his nation at MU20 and MU21 level, has joined the Three Lions ahead of the forthcoming Uefa Nations League fixtures.

“Meanwhile, Ezri Konsa will not be in contention for Croatia at Wembley on Thursday as he continues to follow his own programme but will return to full training later this week before Sunday’s trip to Spain.”

As the statement says, Hill does have experience with England at youth level, making four appearances for the Under-20s between 2021 and 2022 after debuting when he played for Fleetwood, before winning a sole cap for the Under-21s away to Kosovo in June 2022.

He has played 15 times for the Cherries this season, being a staple of their team in both the Premier League and Europa League and helping them to eight straight wins in all competitions heading into the international break.

Meanwhile, Konsa has also featured 15 times for his club this season, admirably standing in for the injured William Saliba to form a fearsome partnership with Gabriel at the heart of Arsenal’s defence, following his £55m summer move from Aston Villa.

Last week, he picked up a knock to his knee during the 2-1 Champions League win over Slavia Prague and was subbed off for Cristhian Mosquera in the 61st minute, although Gunners boss Mikel Arteta insisted afterwards this was simply managing his minutes during a busy period.

In his press conference on Friday ahead of the weekend’s clash with Hull, Arteta brushed off any injury concerns, saying of Konsa: “He’s fine – he was feeling much better today. We took him out on Wednesday for a precaution, but yesterday and today he’s been feeling good.” Konsa would go on to play 90 minutes in the 1-0 victory over the Tigers.

England didn’t specify what his issue was that prompted the call-up of Hill but the Bournemouth man is the second late centre-back addition made by Tuchel after Guehi pulled out of the squad due to injury on Monday – having come off at half-time of Man City’s weekend defeat to Nottingham Forest – leading to the return of Newcastle defender Dan Burn.

It is the first time Burn has been in the Three Lions squad since the World Cup, after being left out for September and October’s games, and he provides another option at the heart of defence alongside Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite, Bayer Leverkusen’s Jarell Quansah and Arsenal’s Ben White, although the latter has been used exclusively as a right-back by the Gunners this season.
